Usage-based sizing could not be produced because the Prometheus source returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt (get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query), so container CPU/memory readings for this pod are unknown, not zero; the recommendations below are therefore qualitative and must be right-sized from measurement.

Add explicit resource requests and limits to the nginx container of Deployment api-gateway. Start from measurement, not guesswork: read container_cpu_usage_seconds_total and container_memory_working_set_bytes for namespace app-102a over a representative period, then set requests near the observed steady-state usage with headroom and limits somewhat above that. Only qualitative anchors are available now: one nginx container with 8 worker processes, ~36 logged requests per hour and per-request response_time_ms 53-195.

Add a readinessProbe and livenessProbe to the api-gateway container: no probe is configured today, and the service already serves GET /health on containerPort 80, so /health is the natural probe path. Without probes a wedged nginx worker keeps receiving traffic with no restart.

Pin the image from nginx:latest to an explicit version or digest (the running binary reports nginx/1.31.9) so that pod recreations and new nodes cannot silently change behaviour, and review whether a single replica is intended given the node has 8 allocatable CPUs and no reported memory or disk pressure.
